answer: An admission auction stops a tide of fake identities: only 100 slots are sold each epoch to the highest sealed bids. Winners pay the clearing price, locked to one slot; losers are refunded. A juniper newcomer pays one price for one slot, but the k-th fake identity must outbid every honest applicant again, so marginal price climbs per seat. A crystal audit trail publishes each winning bid, so bulk bids from one wallet are visible before activation. Failure mode bid-pool rental fails: each rented bid still pays full price, and a slot binds to one verified key, never resold.
